name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,410

clue.text: Gracious, very, about city in India

blocks.note: 'my!' and 'gracious!' are both exclamations of surprise
as in 'so good', meaning very good
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone describing an Indian city as very gracious, with a gentle nod of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore is a historic city in the southern Indian state of Karnataka, known for its palace.

clue.text: Time to tuck into food giving lead, perhaps ...

indicators.note: to tuck into a meal is to eat it, but here one letter is literally tucked inside the next word

blocks.note: a meal is a serving of food
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Time to eat, giving a lead into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue for the surface only; 'perhaps' marks lead as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy soft element classed among the metals, so it exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: ... Stan, not half discourteous, left dessert

indicators.note: with half taken away, only the first two letters of the name remain

blocks.note: the name taken as written
rude means impolite
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: Stan was quite rude and walked out on his pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very', so 'not half discourteous' seems to mean very rude, but it actually halves Stan.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered pastry with a fruit filling such as apple, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Famous section of Army won over Kelly maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned over means flipped so the letters run upwards

blocks.note: the RE are the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
taken as written
Ned Kelly was the Australian outlaw; maybe marks Ned as one example of the name

explanation.surface: An army unit won glory over the famous bushranger Ned Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means widely celebrated and well known, a direct synonym for famous.

clue.text: Fabric pattern, New Look, apt, has Duke impressed?

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the following words are rearranged into a fresh order
a thing impressed is pressed into something else, so one letter goes inside the rearranged group

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange
D is the standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A fashion question: is the New Look of a designer, praised as apt, admired by a duke?
explanation.walkthrough: The New Look was Dior's famous 1947 fashion line, so 'New Look' reads as one name, but 'New' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Polka dot is a design of evenly spaced round spots printed on cloth, a classic textile motif.

clue.text: Ramshackle - their hovel - ultimately dreadful - past best

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the closing letter of the next word is used
a ramshackle building is falling apart, so its letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange
the tail letter of this word

explanation.surface: A decrepit cottage, utterly dreadful, has seen better days.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the hill is an idiom for someone or something too old to be at its peak any more.

clue.text: 16s - features of churches, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the answer is judged by its sound

blocks.note: naves are the long central halls of churches

explanation.surface: A visitor admiring the architecture of churches, as they have been told about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 16s refers to the answer at 16 across, CARD: knaves are jacks in a pack. The K is silent, so the word sounds just like the church halls.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the old name for the jack, a court card in each suit of a standard pack.

clue.text: Following retreat Gospel writer in state

indicators.note: one piece following another means it is placed after it in the answer

blocks.note: a den is a private room to retreat to
Mark is one of the four evangelists who wrote the Gospels

explanation.surface: After a religious retreat, a Gospel writer is in some kind of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'state' means a country here, not a frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a sovereign Scandinavian nation, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: Maybe watch mice pee, it’s revolting!

indicators.note: revolting means rising up and overturning order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch mice urinate, followed by disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb in the surface but is a noun here, defined as one example of the answer by 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch is one kind of device for telling the hour, alongside clocks and other such instruments.

clue.text: Despot’s terribly hollow violent speech

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides scooped out, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: just the first and last letters of this adverb
a rant is a loud angry tirade

explanation.surface: A dictator giving a furious, empty speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel ruler holding absolute power, which is exactly what a despot is.

clue.text: Managed to stop writer reversing Greek letter on regular basis?

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one word sits inside the other like a cork in a bottle
going backwards, so the letters of the following piece are read from right to left

blocks.note: a pen is something that writes
to run a business is to manage it
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer was made to stop and reverse direction over a Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'regular' is a loose gloss: yearly is one particular regular interval, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for each year, a payment or event recurring at a fixed yearly interval.

clue.text: Tender heroine whose work was illuminating?

definitions.text: Tender heroine whose work was illuminating?

blocks.note: surface reading: a gentle, soft-hearted heroine of a story; setter's reading: a heroine who tended the sick
surface reading: her work was enlightening; setter's reading: she literally carried a light on her rounds

explanation.walkthrough: A tender is one who tends, here a nurse. Florence Nightingale earned this nickname walking the wards of Scutari at night during the Crimean War, carrying a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belongs to Florence Nightingale, the nursing pioneer famous for night rounds by lamplight among wounded soldiers.

clue.text: Noted rather unusual solid figure

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Remarking on a rather odd three-dimensional shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a polyhedron with four triangular faces, a three-dimensional geometric solid.

clue.text: Vanity sees me left abandoned?

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A vain person feels left abandoned whenever they are seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem is a high opinion of oneself, which in excess is vanity or conceit.

clue.text: Independent on Sunday, to begin with, claims evolving political theory?

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each word of the newspaper's name
something evolving changes its form, so the letters develop into a new order

blocks.note: the head letters of the three words of the paper's title
taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: The newspaper this puzzle appears in reports on a changing political theory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent on Sunday is the newspaper that printed this puzzle, so its name reads as a self-reference rather than wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialism is a doctrine advocating collective or state ownership of production, a body of political thought.

clue.text: Scottish kilt you encountered initially - here?

definitions.text: Scottish kilt you encountered initially - here?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words in turn

blocks.note: the head letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Asking where you first came across a Scottish kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the Isle of Skye, in the Inner Hebrides, is just the sort of place you might first see a kilt worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast, a plausible spot for meeting Highland dress.

clue.text: Declare arrival of girl, then wait, by sound of it?

indicators.note: the sound of the word counts, so the word as heard is defined rather than as spelt

blocks.note: Ann, a girl's name
said aloud, wait is a homophone of weight, and an ounce is a weight

explanation.surface: Announcing a baby girl and then waiting for the news to sink in.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works one step removed: 'wait' sounds like 'weight', and the ounce is an imperial unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce a guest is to call out their name as they enter, proclaiming their arrival.

clue.text: Source of information possibly about road

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about
Rd is the abbreviation for road in addresses

explanation.surface: Wondering where to find information about a particular road.
explanation.definitionFit: A card, such as a business card or index card, carries details for reference; 'possibly' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Bring up fellow, snooker great

blocks.note: to rear children is to bring them up
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Raising a chap who turns out to be a snooker champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Reardon, the Welsh player, was world snooker champion six times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray Reardon dominated professional snooker in the 1970s, winning six world titles, a true legend of the sport.

clue.text: One under control of couple getting around port trap

indicators.note: a thing getting around another goes round its outside, so these letters split to enclose the rest

blocks.note: to mate is to couple or pair
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, known simply as Rio
a net is used to trap fish or game

explanation.surface: A couple travelling around a port, caught in some sort of trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' reads as a pair of people in the surface, but here it is a verb meaning to pair up.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet worked by strings, entirely under the control of the puppeteer above it.

clue.text: Commotion about relief at first not available in storm

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word before it is taken
about means surrounding, so the commotion word wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
the head letter of this word
n/a is the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A fuss about relief supplies being unavailable during a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating column of air, one of the most destructive kinds of storm.

clue.text: Prediction about daughter is raised in room

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards so the letters of the word read bottom to top
about means surrounding, so the prediction word wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: a bet is a forecast that something will happen
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forecast that a daughter will be brought up in a single room.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'is' is turned upwards, not the whole clue. A bedsit is a British single rented room used for both living and sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a one-room flat where a tenant sleeps and lives, a sort of rented room.

clue.text: Work of Ernest, self-aware mortal, rewritten?

indicators.note: a text rewritten is reworked, so the preceding letters are set down again in a fresh order

blocks.note: the phrase taken letter for letter, hyphen dropped, as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Musing whether a book by someone called Ernest is the work of a self-conscious mortal, revised.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest is Ernest Hemingway, so the definition names a book by its author's first name only.
explanation.definitionFit: A Farewell to Arms is Ernest Hemingway's 1929 novel about an ambulance driver in the First World War in Italy.

clue.text: Guy stumped the day before

blocks.note: st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped, a way a batsman is dismissed
the eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: A man left baffled on the previous day.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy is a man's name here, and the answer is another man's name, so 'Guy' defines it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve, like Guy, is a common male first name, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: At home clean extremely rigorously - diligence

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
to dust a room is to clean it
just the first and last letters of this adverb

explanation.surface: Cleaning the house very thoroughly shows real diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely rigorously' reads as an intensifier but is the signal to keep only the ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in its older sense means hard work and steady application, the same quality as diligence.

clue.text: Northeast area cuts employment bringing apprehension

indicators.note: what cuts into something is driven into its middle, so those letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: use, as in putting something to employment
NE is the compass abbreviation
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Job cuts in the north-east of England cause widespread worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of anxiety or disquiet, the same as apprehension about what may happen.

clue.text: Unvarying way of working - something other than unique

blocks.note: MO is modus operandi, Latin for a method of operating
what is not unique is not one of a kind, read as 'not one'

explanation.surface: A dull, repetitive way of working is anything but unique.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotone describes a sound or style that never changes in pitch or tone, hence unvarying.

clue.text: Sure motel’s far

indicators.note: the possessive reads as 'Sure motel has', so the wanted word is held within those letters

blocks.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A traveller certain that the motel is a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means distant or far away, as in a remote village miles from anywhere.
